why:
rclcpp signals failure by throwing, so it needs no result type. nano-ros builds with -fno-exceptions on Zephyr, FreeRTOS and bare-metal (RFC-0018), so every fallible call returns `nros::Result` and RCLCPP_TRY() early-returns it. The constraint is no exceptions; the type is what replaces them.

phase-428 W5 (2026-09-06) — ledgering a recorded sweep finding. W3 F16(c): the TYPE's existence is a constraint and its NAMESPACE PLACEMENT is not, and the row above only argues the first. RFC-0036 forbids recording a PREFERENCE as a divergence, so this row says which it is rather than leaving the reader to infer it.

`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/result.hpp` declares `namespace rclcpp { using ::nros::Result; }` and says so itself: "`rclcpp::Result` is NOT an upstream rclcpp name — it is a convenience the compat header carried, kept here because step A must not lose anything." Upstream has no `rclcpp::Result`. RFC-0018's exception ban is a real constraint on HAVING an error type; `nros::Result` already satisfies it, so putting our name inside a namespace we do not own buys nothing the constraint requires.

HOW A USER FINDS OUT: SILENTLY WRONG, in the direction that hurts a port most. A file that names `rclcpp::Result` compiles here and fails when moved back to ROS 2, at a symbol whose namespace advertises the opposite. RFC-0089's one-directional consequence is that a ROS 2 file compiles HERE after a mechanical edit — it does not license inventing names in upstream's namespace, which is how the asymmetry stops being legible.

LOCATION CORRECTION for anyone chasing this: it lives in `result.hpp` now, not in the retired `nros/rclcpp_compat.hpp`; a row citing that header is stale. Re-verified by hand against the current worktree before this row was written.

NO DISPOSITION IS WRITTEN on this row. The four dispositions are what clause 1 does to a CANDIDATE FROM CLAUSE 2 (RFC-0089), and `rclcpp::Result` does not exist upstream — it is a name we placed in a namespace we do not own, so there is no upstream item to dispose of. The decision this row is waiting on is whether the alias survives the phase-417 stage-6 rename at all, and entering a disposition here would pre-empt it.

AMENDED 2026-09-07 (phase-427 W8): `Result` is now an ALIAS for `ResultOf<void>` -- one template carries the whole error channel -- and it carries `NROS_NODISCARD`, so dropping a failure on the floor is a diagnostic. The name, the size and the members a caller writes are unchanged.
